title: A Landscaping Lead That Taught Us Something About Nurturing
content:
###  **A Winter Conversation About Spring Plans** 

We once worked with a landscaping company that generated a strong volume of homeowner interest during a winter outreach period. Many of the conversations were with homeowners who were thinking ahead — planning spring projects, not ready to commit in January. 

###  **The Disconnect** 

The company expected every lead to close immediately. When it did not, some leads were treated as failures rather than what they actually were — interest that needed to be revisited when spring planning season arrived. 

###  **What This Revealed** 

It was not a lead generation problem. It was a follow-up and nurturing gap — a system was needed to track and revisit interested homeowners on their own timeline, not the company's. 

### **Why This Matters More Now** 

The market has gotten more competitive. Companies that know how to nurture a lead over weeks or months, rather than expecting instant results, are the ones capturing revenue that others let slip away. 

###  **What We're Building** 

This experience is part of why SIT™ is developing additional support to help clients organize and follow up on leads more effectively — details on that soon.
